kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-01.title: Count the letters
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-01.body:
KANGAROO has 8 letters, so he paints on 8 days. Day 1 is Wednesday; 7 days later, day 8, is again a Wednesday.

**Answer: (C) Wednesday**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-01.title: List the days
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-01.body:
K Wed, A Thu, N Fri, G Sat, A Sun, R Mon, O Tue, O Wed.

**Answer: (C) Wednesday**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-02.title: Add both sides
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-02.body:
Left side: $26 + 8 + 12 = 46$ kg. Right side: $20 + 17 = 37$ kg. The missing stone must weigh $46 - 37 = 9$ kg: stone (C).

**Answer: (C) the 9 kg stone**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-02.title: Pair up stones
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-02.body:
Compare $26$ with $20$: left is 6 more. Compare $12$ with $17$: right is 5 more. So far left is 1 more, plus the 8 kg stone: left is 9 kg heavier.

**Answer: (C) the 9 kg stone**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-03.title: Moves that cancel
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-03.body:
Right then left cancel each other; up then down cancel each other. What is left is the final 'one square right'. So the counter ends one square to the right of where it started, in the same row: picture (B).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-03.title: Walk it step by step
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-03.body:
Starting square → right → up → left (now right above the start) → down (back on the start) → right. The counter is one square right of the start.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-04.title: Add the two times
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-04.body:
From waking up until now: $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours. From now until the train: $3\frac{1}{2}$ hours. Together $1\frac{1}{2} + 3\frac{1}{2} = 5$ hours.

**Answer: (E) Five hours**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-04.title: Use a clock
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-04.body:
Say it is 10:00 now. He woke at 8:30 and the train leaves at 13:30. From 8:30 to 13:30 is 5 hours.

**Answer: (E) Five hours**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-05.title: Use the clues one by one
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-05.body:
Grey shapes: A (square), B (triangle) and E (rectangle). Not a square: A is out. Round or three-sided: the rectangle E is out. Only the grey triangle B is left.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-05.title: Start with the shape
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-05.body:
Round or three-sided: the triangle B or the circle D. The circle D is white, so it must be B, which is grey and not a square.

**Answer: (B) B**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-06.title: Find each price
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-06.body:
One scoop: 150 cents ÷ 3 = 50 cents. One bar: 240 cents ÷ 2 = 120 cents. Together $50 + 120 = 170$ cents = 1 € 70 c.

**Answer: (A) 1 € 70 c**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-07.title: Full hours and half hours
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-07.body:
Full hours in the time: 8, 9, 10, giving $27$ rings. Half hours: 8:30, 9:30, 10:30, giving 3 rings. $27 + 3 = 30$.

**Answer: (D) 30 times**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-08.title: Count squares and half squares
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-08.body:
Count whole grid squares, and count two half squares (triangles cut by a diagonal) as one square:
- (A): 10 squares.
- (B): 11 squares.
- (C): 12 squares.
- (D): a $4 \times 2$ rectangle (8) plus a point (1): 9 squares.
- (E): a $2 \times 4$ rectangle (8) plus a point (1): 9 squares.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-08.title: Cut and move pieces
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-08.body:
In (C), the four triangular points can be moved to fill a $2 \times 2$ square in the middle plus a ring around it — it fits exactly 12 squares. (D) and (E) are clearly only 9 squares, and (A) and (B) are like (C) with pieces missing.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-09.title: Use big boxes first
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-09.body:
Five boxes of 12 hold 60 eggs, and the last 6 eggs go in one small box: $5 + 1 = 6$ boxes.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-09.title: Why not 5?
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-09.body:
Five boxes hold at most $5 \times 12 = 60 < 66$ eggs. So 6 boxes is the least.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-10.title: Account for the pets
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-10.body:
- 2 children with dog + fish: uses 2 dogs and both fish.
- 3 children with cat + dog: uses 3 cats and 3 dogs.
- Dogs left: $6 - 5 = 1$, held by 1 more child (only that dog).
- Cats left: $8 - 3 = 5$. No child has two cats, and no fish or dogs are left to pair them with, so 5 children with one cat each.

Total: $2 + 3 + 1 + 5 = 11$.

**Answer: (A) 11**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-10.title: Count pets per child
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-10.body:
There are $8 + 6 + 2 = 16$ pets. The 5 children with two pets have 10 of them. The other 6 pets (5 cats and 1 dog) must each belong to a different child, because no pairs are possible. $5 + 6 = 11$ children.

**Answer: (A) 11**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-11.title: Smallest possible total
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-11.body:
The least he can have is 13 coins of 5 c: $13 \times 5 = 65$ c. So 60 c is impossible.

**Answer: (B) 60 c**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-11.title: Check the others
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-11.body:
Each 10 c coin instead of a 5 c coin adds 5 c, so every multiple of 5 from 65 c to 130 c works: 70 c (1 ten), 80 c (3 tens), 115 c (10 tens), 125 c (12 tens). Only 60 c is below the minimum.

**Answer: (B) 60 c**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-12.title: Mirror the grey squares
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-12.body:
Folding flips the left side onto the right like a mirror: the column next to the line lands on the first column to the right, the second column on the second, the third on the third.
- Row 2: grey in columns 2 and 3 on the left → covers B and A.
- Row 4: grey in columns 3 and 2 counted from the line → covers D and the square next to it.
- Row 5: grey in the third column from the line → covers C.

In row 5 the second column from the line on the left is white, so E stays uncovered.

**Answer: (E) E**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-12.title: Check E directly
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-12.body:
E is in the bottom row, second square to the right of the line. The square that lands on it is the bottom row, second square to the left of the line, which is white. So E is not covered.

**Answer: (E) E**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-13.title: Use the multiples
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-13.body:
Anna's number is a multiple of 2 and of 3, so it is 6. Then Bob has 3 and Cleo has 2. Dido is 4 times Eva: only $4 = 4 \times 1$ works. The numbers 6, 3, 2, 4, 1 are used, so Ferdl rolled 5.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-13.title: Who can roll 5?
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-13.body:
5 is not double, triple or four times any die number, and neither $5 \times 2$, $5 \times 3$ nor $5 \times 4$ is on a die. So 5 cannot be rolled by Anna, Bob, Cleo, Dido or Eva — it must be Ferdl's.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-14.title: Correct minus wrong
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-14.body:
She gained 4 points overall, so (correct) − (wrong) = 4 and (correct) + (wrong) = 10. That gives 7 correct and 3 wrong.

**Answer: (D) 3**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-14.title: Start from all correct
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-14.body:
All 10 correct would give 20 points. Each wrong answer changes +1 into −1, costing 2 points. $20 - 14 = 6$ points lost, so $6 \div 2 = 3$ wrong answers.

**Answer: (D) 3**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-15.title: Find a long path and the blocked parts
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-15.body:
Number the rows 1–7 from the top and the columns 1–7 from the left; Ronnie enters at the top-left square and leaves at the bottom-right square.

Some parts of the maze are dead ends (pockets with only one opening): if Ronnie goes in, he has to come out through the same square, which is not allowed. Exploring the maze, the best route visits these squares:

row 1 col 1 → down to row 2 → right along row 2 to col 4 → down to row 4 → left to col 3 → up to row 3 → left to col 2 → down to row 4 → left to col 1 → down to row 6 → right → down to row 7 → right to col 3 → up to row 5 → right along row 5 to col 6 → up to row 3 → left to col 5 → up to row 1 → right to col 7 → down column 7 to row 6 → left → down → right to the exit.

That is 37 squares. The 12 squares it misses lie in side branches: going into any of them would either trap Ronnie in a dead end or cut him off from the rest of his route, so no path can collect more than 37 pieces.

**Answer: (C) 37**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-16.title: Count the pieces
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-16.body:
Each cake: $4 \times 3 = 12$ pieces. Two cakes: 24 pieces. 3 were left, so $24 - 3 = 21$ people.

**Answer: (B) 21**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-16.title: Draw it
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-16.body:
Draw a cake cut into 4, then each quarter into 3: 12 pieces. Double for two cakes: 24. Cross out 3 leftover pieces: 21.

**Answer: (B) 21**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-17.title: Undo the swaps backwards
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-17.body:
End: Masha, Sasha, Dasha, Pasha.
- Undo the Dasha–Pasha swap: Masha, Sasha, **Pasha, Dasha**.
- Undo the Masha–Dasha swap: **Dasha**, Sasha, Pasha, **Masha**.

**Answer: (C) Dasha, Sasha, Pasha, Masha**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-17.title: Check forwards
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-17.body:
Start: Dasha, Sasha, Pasha, Masha. Masha↔Dasha: Masha, Sasha, Pasha, Dasha. Dasha↔Pasha: Masha, Sasha, Dasha, Pasha ✓.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-18.title: List them
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-18.body:
The clock goes from 00:00 to 23:59. Four equal digits: 00:00, 11:11, 22:22. (33:33, 44:44, ... are not times.)

**Answer: (C) 3 times**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-18.title: Look at the hours
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-18.body:
The hour must be two equal digits: 00, 11 or 22 (33 and above don't exist). The minutes must repeat the same digit, and 00, 11, 22 are all valid minutes. So 3 times.

**Answer: (C) 3 times**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-19.title: Opposite faces
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-19.body:
From behind we see the faces opposite to the front faces, and left and right are swapped.
- Front faces: left die 5, bottom middle 3, top die 3, right die 2.
- Back faces: $7 - 5 = 2$, $7 - 3 = 4$, $7 - 3 = 4$, $7 - 2 = 5$.

So from behind: top die 4, bottom row from left to right 5, 4, 2 (the right die now appears on the left). The tops still show 1. Only picture (C) shows this.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-19.title: Rule out by one die
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-19.body:
Look only at the die that was on the right with 2 at the front: from behind it is on the left and shows 5. Then check the middle bottom die, which must show 4 from behind, and the far-right die, which must show 2. Only (C) has all of these.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-20.title: Turn the cards
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-20.body:
The cards are 6, 8 and 9, and a 6 turned upside down is a 9 (and the other way round). So two of the cards can each show 6 or 9; the 8 is always 8.
- The 8 can be in 3 places.
- Each of the other two places can show 6 or 9: $2 \times 2 = 4$ ways.

$3 \times 4 = 12$ numbers.

**Answer: (E) 12**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-21.title: Count triangles
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-21.body:
The pattern is three hexagons, each made of 6 small triangles: 18 triangles. The tiles have (A) 6, (B) 2, (C) 6, (D) 5 and (E) 3 triangles. Identical tiles must split 18 evenly, and 18 cannot be split into 5s. So tile (D) is impossible.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-21.title: Check that the others fit
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-21.body:
(A): 3 hexagons. (B): each hexagon is 3 rhombi. (E): each hexagon is 2 trapezoids. (C) can also be placed 3 times. Only (D), with 5 triangles, cannot work because $18 \div 5$ is not whole.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-22.title: Wall plus towers
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-22.body:
The wall goes round a square that is 7 cubes long on each side. One layer of the wall has $7 + 7 + 5 + 5 = 24$ cubes. The wall is 2 layers high: $48$ cubes. On top stand 8 single cubes (the battlements). Total $48 + 8 = 56$.

**Answer: (A) 56**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-22.title: Subtract the hole
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-22.body:
A full $7 \times 7$ layer has 49 cubes; the empty middle is $5 \times 5 = 25$, so the ring has $49 - 25 = 24$ cubes. Two layers: 48, plus 8 battlement cubes: 56.

**Answer: (A) 56**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-23.title: Fill in the circles
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-23.body:
8 is in the top-left corner, 6 in the middle of the right side and 7 in the middle of the bottom side. Call the other corners top-right $a$, bottom-right $b$, bottom-left $c$.
- Right side: $a + 6 + b = 13$, so $a + b = 7$.
- Bottom side: $c + 7 + b = 13$, so $b + c = 6$.
- Top side: $8 + (\text{top middle}) + a = 13$, so top middle $= 5 - a$.

Trying the numbers 1–5: $a = 2$, $b = 5$, $c = 1$, top middle 3, left middle 4 works. The grey circles are the four corners: $8 + 2 + 5 + 1 = 16$.

**Answer: (E) 16**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-23.title: Add all four sides
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-23.body:
Adding the four sides gives $4 \times 13 = 52$. This counts the middle circles once and the corners twice. All eight numbers add up to $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 = 36$. So the corners are counted once more: corners $= 52 - 36 = 16$.

**Answer: (E) 16**

kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-24.title: Add a ring each time
kangaroo-at-2011-ecolier-24.body:
The patterns have 1, 7 and 19 hexagons. Each new pattern adds a ring around the old one: 6, 12, 18, 24, ... hexagons. Pattern 4: $19 + 18 = 37$. Pattern 5: $37 + 24 = 61$.

**Answer: (D) 61**
